A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. Every open document costs an instance threads and memory
(`tools/proof/README.md`, "Relaunch the instance between proof sessions", has
the measured cost and what closing one gives back): a proof that closes what
it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and one that does not
relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument. A mutant's anchor is counted by `tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py` in
  `make test`: a proof taking `--mutant` holds its mutants in a top-level
  table (tree text as file, anchor, replacement; switches as names), and a new
  table shape or a mutant with no tree text gets its row there in the same
  change, and a table's expression stays pure, because the check evaluates it.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. Its scale is
`-RCDevCaptureScale 1|2|3` (spec §11 #539), which `screens.py` pins to 2, so a
capture is 2× on a 1× display without moving a window. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A proof that
compares with the base's built APP (`co2a_proof.py` D15, `ramp_proof.py` U1)
finds its base with `tree_copy.default_base()` and builds it whole with
`tree_copy.make_base_copy`; it never pins a commit's `app/` against the
tree's core. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Tips (spec §11 TIP-1…TIP-7): what the dialog links to, when Frame Job asks
4	/// by itself, and what it remembers. Foundation only, so a probe can run the
5	/// rule against a clock of its own and the AppKit-free export queue can be
6	/// followed from here. The dialog is `TipsWindowController.swift`, the
7	/// editor's button `TipsToolbarButton.swift`, Settings' pane
8	/// `TipsSettingsPane.swift`.
9	
10	/// The one address "Leave a Tip" opens (TIP-1). The page is the owner's.
11	enum TipsLink {
12	    static let url = "https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/"
13	}
14	
15	/// What the schedule is decided from: the stored state, read at one moment.
16	struct TipsState: Equatable {
17	    /// When the first counted export succeeded; nil before one has.
18	    var firstExport: Date?
19	    /// How many exports a person confirmed in the export card have succeeded.
20	    var exports = 0
21	    /// When the automatic ask was last shown, or "Leave a Tip" last pressed.
22	    var lastAsked: Date?
23	    /// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle.
24	    var enabled = true
25	}
26	
27	/// When the automatic ask is due (TIP-3). Pure: the state, a moment and a
28	/// calendar in, a Bool out.
29	enum TipsSchedule {
30	    static let firstAskDays = 30
31	    static let firstAskExports = 5
32	    static let skipMonths = 6
33	
34	    /// The Gregorian calendar in the Mac's time zone as it is now, whatever
35	    /// calendar the person's Mac shows: "December" is its month 12.
36	    static func localCalendar() -> Calendar {
37	        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
38	        calendar.timeZone = TimeZone.current
39	        return calendar
40	    }
41	
42	    /// Off is never due. The first ask waits for `firstAskExports` exports
43	    /// and `firstAskDays` days since the first of them. After an ask, only a
44	    /// December is due, and not one whose 1 December 00:00 is less than
45	    /// `skipMonths` calendar months after the last ask.
46	    static func isDue(_ state: TipsState, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Bool {
47	        guard state.enabled else { return false }
48	        guard let first = state.firstExport else { return false }
49	        guard state.exports >= firstAskExports else { return false }
50	        guard now.timeIntervalSince(first) >= Double(firstAskDays) * 86_400 else { return false }
51	        guard let last = state.lastAsked else { return true }
52	        guard calendar.component(.month, from: now) == 12 else { return false }
53	        let year = calendar.component(.year, from: now)
54	        guard
55	            let december = calendar.date(from: DateComponents(year: year, month: 12, day: 1)),
56	            let earliest = calendar.date(byAdding: .month, value: skipMonths, to: last)
57	        else { return false }
58	        return earliest <= december
59	    }
60	}
61	
62	/// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle (TIP-5, TIP-6): on shows the editor's Tips button
63	/// and lets the automatic ask happen.
64	enum TipsSettings {
65	    /// Bool; absent = true.
66	    static let enabledKey = "FrameJobTips"
67	
68	    /// Posted after the toggle is written, so every editor's Tips button
69	    /// follows it at once.
70	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name("FrameJobTipsSettingsDidChange")
71	
72	    static func isEnabled(in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> Bool {
73	        defaults.object(forKey: enabledKey) == nil ? true : defaults.bool(forKey: enabledKey)
74	    }
75	
76	    /// Writes the toggle and posts `didChangeNotification`.
77	    static func setEnabled(_ enabled: Bool, in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) {
78	        defaults.set(enabled, forKey: enabledKey)
79	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: didChangeNotification, object: nil)
80	    }
81	}
82	
83	/// The stored state and its three writers (TIP-5). Every writer is reached
84	/// only from a person's door: an export confirmed in the export card, or the
85	/// dialog's "Leave a Tip". Main thread.
86	final class TipsAsk {
87	    /// Int; absent = 0.
88	    static let exportsKey = "FrameJobTipsExports"
89	    /// A date, stamped by the first counted export and never again.
90	    static let firstExportKey = "FrameJobTipsFirstExport"
91	    /// A date: the last automatic ask, or the last press of "Leave a Tip".
92	    static let lastAskedKey = "FrameJobTipsLastAsked"
93	
94	    /// The app's own, over the bundle's defaults and the real clock.
95	    static let shared = TipsAsk()
96	
97	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
98	    private let now: () -> Date
99	    private let calendar: () -> Calendar
100	
101	    init(
102	        defaults: UserDefaults = .standard, now: @escaping () -> Date = { Date() },
103	        calendar: @escaping () -> Calendar = { TipsSchedule.localCalendar() }
104	    ) {
105	        self.defaults = defaults
106	        self.now = now
107	        self.calendar = calendar
108	    }
109	
110	    var state: TipsState {
111	        TipsState(
112	            firstExport: defaults.object(forKey: Self.firstExportKey) as? Date,
113	            exports: defaults.integer(forKey: Self.exportsKey),
114	            lastAsked: defaults.object(forKey: Self.lastAskedKey) as? Date,
115	            enabled: TipsSettings.isEnabled(in: defaults))
116	    }
117	
118	    /// One more export a person confirmed has succeeded. Counts whatever the
119	    /// toggle says.
120	    func countExport() {
121	        let state = self.state
122	        defaults.set(state.exports + 1, forKey: Self.exportsKey)
123	        if state.firstExport == nil { defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.firstExportKey) }
124	    }
125	
126	    /// True when the automatic ask is due now, and then it is recorded as
127	    /// asked, so the caller shows the dialog and a second call answers false.
128	    func takeAsk() -> Bool {
129	        let moment = now()
130	        guard TipsSchedule.isDue(state, now: moment, calendar: calendar()) else { return false }
131	        defaults.set(moment, forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
132	        return true
133	    }
134	
135	    /// "Leave a Tip" was pressed, from any door: that is an ask too.
136	    func noteTipPageOpened() {
137	        defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
138	    }
139	}
140	
141	/// Which export queue jobs a person started (Add to Queue), followed by id as
142	/// `AgentExports` follows the agent's, so the queue's jobs carry no origin
143	/// (TIP-4). `settle()` runs on every change of the queue.
144	final class TipsQueueFollower {
145	    private let state: (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?
146	    private let completed: () -> Void
147	    private(set) var followed: Set<UInt64> = []
148	
149	    init(state: @escaping (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?, completed: @escaping () -> Void)
150	    {
151	        self.state = state
152	        self.completed = completed
153	    }
154	
155	    func follow(_ id: UInt64) {
156	        followed.insert(id)
157	        settle()
158	    }
159	
160	    /// A followed job that completed calls `completed` once and is dropped;
161	    /// one cancelled, failed or gone from the list is dropped; one waiting or
162	    /// running stays.
163	    func settle() {
164	        for id in followed.sorted() {
165	            switch state(id) {
166	            case .completed:
167	                followed.remove(id)
168	                completed()
169	            case .cancelled, .failed, nil:
170	                followed.remove(id)
171	            case .waiting, .running:
172	                break
173	            }
174	        }
175	    }
176	}

3	/// Settings' Tips pane (spec §11 TIP-6): the window's last. A bare heading,
4	/// one visible sentence, the toggle and a Tips button.
5	///
6	/// **The toggle** (`TipsSettings`, on by default) decides two things at once:
7	/// whether the editor shows its Tips button, and whether Frame Job ever shows
8	/// the dialog by itself. It saves when it is pressed, with no Save button, and
9	/// every open editor follows `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`.
10	///
11	/// **The button is always there.** It shows the dialog whatever the toggle
12	/// says, and is never hidden or disabled: with the toggle off it is the one
13	/// way left to reach the dialog. What it shows is a parameter, so a probe
14	/// presses it without a window appearing.
15	///
16	/// **No ⓘ.** The sentence is short enough to show (under SH-5's 200
17	/// characters), and the dialog one press away says the rest. It is a
18	/// person's setting: no tool reads or writes it (R6-12, MC-7).
19	final class TipsSettingsPane: NSStackView {
20	    static let paneTitle = "Tips"
21	    static let blurb = "Frame Job is free and open source, made by one developer. Tips are voluntary."
22	    static let toggleTitle = "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder"
23	    static let buttonTitle = "Tips"
24	    /// The Settings window's width less its two insets.
25	    private static let textWidth: CGFloat = 420
26	
27	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
28	    private let showTips: () -> Void
29	
30	    let headingLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: TipsSettingsPane.paneTitle)
31	    let blurbLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: TipsSettingsPane.blurb)
32	    let toggleBox = NSButton(
33	        checkboxWithTitle: TipsSettingsPane.toggleTitle, target: nil, action: nil)
34	    private(set) var tipsButton: NSButton!
35	
36	    init(defaults: UserDefaults, showTips: @escaping () -> Void) {
37	        self.defaults = defaults
38	        self.showTips = showTips
39	        super.init(frame: .zero)
40	        build()
41	        sync()
42	    }
43	
44	    @available(*, unavailable)
45	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
46	        fatalError("TipsSettingsPane does not support NSCoder")
47	    }
48	
49	    private func build() {
50	        headingLabel.font = DS.sans(15, weight: .bold)
51	        headingLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
52	        headingLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.heading")
53	
54	        blurbLabel.font = DS.sans(13)
55	        blurbLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
56	        blurbLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = Self.textWidth
57	        blurbLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.blurb")
58	
59	        toggleBox.font = DS.sans(13)
60	        toggleBox.target = self
61	        toggleBox.action = #selector(toggled(_:))
62	        toggleBox.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.toggle")
63	
64	        tipsButton = StickerButton(
65	            title: Self.buttonTitle, style: .secondary, target: self,
66	            action: #selector(tipsClicked(_:)))
67	        tipsButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.button")
68	
69	        orientation = .vertical
70	        alignment = .leading
71	        spacing = 12
72	        for view in [headingLabel, blurbLabel, toggleBox, tipsButton] as [NSView] {
73	            addArrangedSubview(view)
74	        }
75	    }
76	
77	    /// The stored toggle on the box. Reads only.
78	    func sync() {
79	        toggleBox.state = TipsSettings.isEnabled(in: defaults) ? .on : .off
80	    }
81

3	/// The Tips dialog (spec §11 TIP-1, TIP-2): who a tip funds, "Leave a Tip"
4	/// and "Not Now".
5	///
6	/// **A window and not a sheet, deliberately.** It has three doors — the
7	/// editor's Tips button, Settings' Tips button and the automatic ask — and
8	/// two of them have no document to hold a sheet. It is modal to nothing, so
9	/// no window and no tool call ever waits on it. `SettingsWindowController`'s
10	/// mould: one instance, not released when closed, no frame autosave name.
11	/// It is built from the sheets' own pieces so it reads as one of them, and
12	/// it is left out of the Window menu because both buttons reopen it.
13	///
14	/// **Two ways to show it.** `show()` is a person's press: key and front, and
15	/// it writes nothing. `showAutomatic()` is the ask Frame Job makes by itself
16	/// (TIP-4): front WITHOUT key, so a Return typed into the editor can never
17	/// press "Leave a Tip". The two order calls are closures because a probe's
18	/// window is never key and could not tell the two apart otherwise.
19	///
20	/// **What "Leave a Tip" does.** Opens `TipsLink.url` in the browser, records
21	/// the press as an ask (TIP-5) and closes. Nothing here knows whether anyone
22	/// tipped.
23	final class TipsWindowController: NSWindowController {
24	    /// The app's one Tips dialog. A probe builds its own.
25	    static let shared = TipsWindowController()
26	
27	    static let windowTitle = "Tips"
28	    static let heading = "Frame Job is free and open source"
29	    static let body =
30	        "Frame Job is made by one developer. It is free to use and its source is open. If it "
31	        + "is useful to you, a tip helps pay for the time to keep working on it. Tips are "
32	        + "voluntary, and nothing in Frame Job is locked without one."
33	    static let hint = "You can turn this reminder off in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips."
34	    static let notNowTitle = "Not Now"
35	    static let tipTitle = "Leave a Tip"
36	
37	    private let ask: TipsAsk
38	    private let open: (URL) -> Void
39	    private let orderKey: (NSWindow) -> Void
40	    private let orderFront: (NSWindow) -> Void
41	
42	    private(set) var notNowButton: NSButton!
43	    private(set) var tipButton: NSButton!
44	
45	    init(
46	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
47	        open: @escaping (URL) -> Void = { NSWorkspace.shared.open($0) },
48	        orderKey: @escaping (NSWindow) -> Void = { $0.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil) },
49	        orderFront: @escaping (NSWindow) -> Void = { $0.orderFront(nil) }
50	    ) {
51	        self.ask = ask
52	        self.open = open
53	        self.orderKey = orderKey
54	        self.orderFront = orderFront
55	        let window = NSWindow(
56	            contentRect: NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: sheetWidth, height: 240),
57	            styleMask: [.titled, .closable], backing: .buffered, defer: false)
58	        window.title = Self.windowTitle
59	        window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false
60	        window.isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true
61	        super.init(window: window)
62	        let content = buildContent()
63	        window.contentView = content
64	        window.setContentSize(content.fittingSize)
65	        window.center()
66	        applyBackground()
67	    }
68	
69	    @available(*, unavailable)
70	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
71	        fatalError("TipsWindowController does not support NSCoder")
72	    }
73	
74	    private func buildContent() -> NSView {
75	        let width = sheetWidth - sheetInset * 2
76	        let bodyLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: Self.body)
77	        bodyLabel.font = DS.sans(13)
78	        bodyLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
79	        bodyLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = width
80	        bodyLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.body")

83	        hintLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
84	        hintLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
85	        hintLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = width
86	        hintLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.hint")

98	            title: Self.heading, content: sheetColumn([bodyLabel, hintLabel]),
99	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(cancel: notNowButton, apply: tipButton))
100	    }
101	
102	    private func applyBackground() {
103	        window?.backgroundColor = DS.chromeBackground
104	        window?.contentView?.layer?.backgroundColor = DS.chromeBackground.cgColor
105	    }
106	
107	    // MARK: - Showing

109	    /// A person's press of a Tips button: key and front. Writes nothing.

136	// MARK: - The export doors
137	
138	/// The two places a person's export reaches Tips (TIP-4): the Export… sheet's
139	/// success and an Add to Queue job. `EditorViewController+Export.swift` is
140	/// the only caller; the agent's `export` never comes here. The ask, the
141	/// dialog and the queue are parameters so a probe runs both doors on its own.
142	/// Main thread.
143	final class TipsDoors {
144	    static let shared = TipsDoors()
145	
146	    private let ask: TipsAsk
147	    private let dialog: () -> TipsWindowController
148	    private let queue: ExportQueueController
149	    private var follower: TipsQueueFollower?
150	    private var queueObserver: NSObjectProtocol?
151	    /// The result sheets still up after a counted success, each waiting for
152	    /// its window's sheet to end.
153	    private var sheetEnds: [TipsSheetEnd] = []
154	
155	    init(
156	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
157	        dialog: @escaping () -> TipsWindowController = { TipsWindowController.shared },
158	        queue: ExportQueueController = .shared
159	    ) {
160	        self.ask = ask
161	        self.dialog = dialog
162	        self.queue = queue
163	    }
164	
165	    deinit {
166	        if let queueObserver { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(queueObserver) }
167	    }
168	
169	    /// An Export… the person confirmed has succeeded: counted now. The ask
170	    /// waits until `window`'s sheet — the export's own result panel — ends,
171	    /// and one main-queue turn more so the sheet has left; with no sheet
172	    /// attached it is asked at once.
173	    func exportSucceeded(sheetOn window: NSWindow?) {
174	        ask.countExport()
175	        guard let window, window.attachedSheet != nil else {
176	            askIfDue()
177	            return
178	        }
179	        sheetEnds.append(
180	            TipsSheetEnd(window: window) { [weak self] watch in
181	                guard let self else { return }
182	                self.sheetEnds.removeAll { $0 === watch }
183	                self.askIfDue()
184	            })
185	    }
186	
187	    /// An Add to Queue job the person confirmed: followed to its end by id.
188	    /// A completion counts and asks; a cancel or a failure does neither.
189	    func follow(queueJob id: UInt64) {
190	        if follower == nil {
191	            follower = TipsQueueFollower(
192	                state: { [queue] in queue.job($0)?.state },
193	                completed: { [weak self] in
194	                    self?.ask.countExport()
195	                    self?.askIfDue()
196	                })
197	            queueObserver = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
198	                forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification, object: queue, queue: nil
199	            ) { [weak self] _ in self?.follower?.settle() }
200	        }
201	        follower?.follow(id)
202	    }
203	
204	    /// Shows the dialog when the schedule says so, recording the ask at the
205	    /// moment it is shown.
206	    private func askIfDue() {
207	        guard ask.takeAsk() else { return }
208	        dialog().showAutomatic()
209	    }
210	}
211	
212	/// One wait for a window's sheet to end, then one main-queue turn.
213	private final class TipsSheetEnd: NSObject {
214	    private let then: (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void
215	
216	    init(window: NSWindow, then: @escaping (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void) {
217	        self.then = then
218	        super.init()
219	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
220	            self, selector: #selector(ended(_:)), name: NSWindow.didEndSheetNotification,
221	            object: window)
222	    }
223	
224	    @objc private func ended(_ note: Notification) {
225	        NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(self)
226	        DispatchQueue.main.async { self.then(self) }
227	    }
228	}

231	
232	/// The command half, at the foot of the file that owns the feature
233	/// (`SettingsWindowController.swift`'s precedent): a nil-target selector, so

235	extension AppDelegate {
236	    @objc func showTips(_ sender: Any?) {
237	        TipsWindowController.shared.show()
238	    }
239	}

413	# Spec §11 — decisions: Tips
414	
415	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
416	[`README.md`](README.md).
417	
418	These were made with no road map, from the owner's words of 2026-11-14: a tips dialog, a green
419	Tips button to the right of Export in the editor, an automatic ask on a usage-then-calendar
420	schedule, and a Settings section that turns the ask and the button off. The owner called the
421	button an experiment that may be removed.
422	
423	- **TIP-1 — A tip is voluntary, nothing in Frame Job is gated on one, and the app holds no payment
424	  code: the dialog says who a tip funds and opens one web page.** The statement is plain: Frame
425	  Job is made by one developer, it is free to use and its source is open, a tip helps pay for the
426	  time to keep working on it, and nothing is locked without one. "Leave a Tip" opens
427	  `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/` in the person's browser, and that address is ONE
428	  constant (`TipsLink.url`, `Tips.swift`), so moving the page is a one-line change. The page is
429	  the owner's to make. Frame Job never learns whether anyone tipped, so there is no "thank you"
430	  state and nothing to restore. Risk accepted: until the page exists the button opens a missing
431	  page.
432	- **TIP-2 — The dialog is its own small window titled "Tips", not a sheet and not an app-modal
433	  alert, and it has three doors: the editor's Tips button, Settings' Tips button and the automatic
434	  ask.** A sheet needs a host window and two of the doors have no document (Settings, and Settings
435	  opened from the Welcome window); an app-modal alert would stop every window and would sit in
436	  front of an MCP client's calls. A window that is modal to nothing cannot make anything wait. It
437	  is the Settings window's mould (`TipsWindowController`): one instance, not released when closed,
438	  no frame autosave name (so it writes no `NSWindow Frame` key), built from the sheets' own pieces
439	  (`makeSheetView`, `makeButtonRow`) so it reads as one of them, Escape on "Not Now" and Return on
440	  "Leave a Tip". It is left out of the Window menu: a two-button dialog is not a place to come
441	  back to, and both buttons reopen it. There is no menu item for it, and no MCP mirror, because
442	  showing it is not an edit (spec §7.9).
443	- **TIP-3 — The automatic ask is due by usage first and the calendar after: never while the
444	  toggle is off; first once at least 5 exports are counted AND at least 30 × 24 hours have passed
445	  since the first counted export; after an ask, only in a December, and a December is skipped
446	  whole when its 1 December 00:00 is less than six calendar months after the last ask.** The rule
447	  is one pure function, `TipsSchedule.isDue(_:now:calendar:)`, over the stored state, the moment
448	  and a calendar. "30 days of use" counts from the first counted export and not from the first
449	  launch: a launch is also what `framejob-mcp` and every proof make, and a date stamped at launch
450	  would count use by agents alone. It is elapsed time, not thirty separate days of use, which
451	  would make an occasional user wait a year. "December" is month 12 of the GREGORIAN calendar in
452	  the Mac's current time zone (`TipsSchedule.localCalendar()`, built at each evaluation), whatever
453	  calendar the person's Mac shows, so the same instant can be December in Auckland and November
454	  in Los Angeles. A December is judged whole so that an ask on 30 June cannot bring the next one
455	  on 30 December: a last ask after 1 June 00:00 skips that year's December, and one at or before
456	  it does not. A clock set back before the last ask or the first export makes nothing due. Risk
457	  accepted: the rule is evaluated only when a counted export completes (TIP-4), so a person who
458	  exports nothing in December is not asked that year.
459	- **TIP-4 — Only an export a person confirmed in the export card counts, and only its completion
460	  evaluates the ask; the agent's `export` never does either.** The card's two commits both sit
461	  behind its save panel (`ExportSheetCommit.swift`), which no tool and no dev switch answers:
462	  Export… (`EditorViewController.beginExport`) and Add to Queue (`enqueueExport`). The first hands
463	  the progress sheet an `onSuccess` it calls once, on a success only; the second follows its job
464	  by the id `enqueue` answered (`TipsQueueFollower`, `AgentExports`' pattern), so
465	  `ExportQueueController` is not changed and its jobs carry no origin. The agent's `export`
466	  enqueues on the same queue and is never followed, and the Assistant tab's `export` is that same
467	  door. So an instance driven only by an MCP client, the assistant or a proof counts nothing,
468	  writes no key and is never shown the dialog, which is what keeps `mcp.py`'s `DEFAULTS MOVED`
469	  guard quiet. A counted export is counted when it succeeds. The ask is evaluated, and recorded,
470	  at the moment it is shown: for Export…, when the result sheet ends (Close or Show in Finder),
471	  one main-queue turn later; for a queued job, when it completes. The automatic ask is ordered
472	  front WITHOUT becoming key, so a Return typed into the editor can never press "Leave a Tip";
473	  the two buttons' doors make it key. Risks accepted: after Show in Finder the dialog appears
474	  behind Finder and is found on return; a window closed with its result sheet still attached
475	  never ends that sheet, so that export is counted and the ask waits for the next one.
476	- **TIP-5 — The state is four keys of the bundle's defaults domain, written only at a person's
477	  doors.** `FrameJobTips` (Bool, absent means on) is the toggle, written by Settings' checkbox.
478	  `FrameJobTipsExports` (Int) and `FrameJobTipsFirstExport` (a date, stamped once) are written
479	  when a counted export succeeds, and counting goes on while the toggle is off, so turning it back
480	  on behaves sensibly. `FrameJobTipsLastAsked` (a date) is written when the automatic ask is shown
481	  and when "Leave a Tip" is pressed from any door: someone who has just visited the page is not
482	  asked again that December. Opening the dialog by hand and choosing "Not Now", or closing it,
483	  writes nothing. Dates are stored as dates, so `defaults write … -date` sets one. No project
484	  format changes. Risk accepted: the state is per Mac and per build identity, so a Debug build
485	  and a reinstall on another Mac each start again.
486	- **TIP-6 — The editor's Tips button is an `AccentButton` filled with `DS.tips` (`#2E7D32`), right
487	  of Export…, and Settings ▸ Tips holds the toggle that removes it.** The owner asked for green.
488	  The fill is a fixed leaf green, the same in both appearances as the recorder's coral Record
489	  button is, with the white `DS.onAccent` label at 5.1:1. It is deliberately not `DS.action` and
490	  not `DS.forest`: CI-4 keeps mint for the action ink and nothing else, and forest (`#1F8564`) is
491	  within 10/255 of the action ink's light value (`#1E8F6E`), so a forest button would read as an
492	  action in the light appearance. `DS.tips` sits about 40° of hue from both action values, so
493	  CI-4 stands unamended. How it looks is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`. The button is 12 pt
494	  after Export… with no rule between them, has no symbol, and is `TipsToolbarButton`, a view that
495	  hides itself while the toggle is off and follows `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`, so the
496	  frozen editor file holds nothing for it: removing the experiment is deleting that file and one
497	  line of `buildToolbar`. Settings' fifth and last pane, "Tips", is a bare heading, one visible
498	  sentence (under SH-5's and `settings_layout_probe` L5's 200 characters, so it needs no ⓘ), the
499	  checkbox "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder" (on by default) and a "Tips" button.
500	  Unticking stops the automatic ask and removes the button from every open editor at once; the
501	  pane's own button is never hidden or disabled and shows the dialog whatever the toggle says. It
502	  is a person's setting: no tool reads or writes it (R6-12, MC-7).
503	- **TIP-7 — The feature has no `-RCDev` switch and no dev tool, and its proof is a probe.**
504	  `tools/proof/tips_proof.py` builds `tips_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` and hands the schedule
505	  its clock, calendar and a scratch defaults suite; the two export doors are run for real, on a
506	  document made in process, with the ask, the window and the queue injected (`TipsDoors`), and the
507	  window's two order calls are closures so "front, not key" can be read where no probe window is
508	  ever key. A person pins state with `defaults write` (`docs/manual-checks.md`). So Debug, Release
509	  and Distribution run the same code. The offscreen harness pins `FrameJobTips` OFF: older chrome
510	  proofs read the toolbar at fixed points (`sharp_chrome.py`'s `EXPORT_RIGHT`,
511	  `phase7_chrome.py`'s accent patch) and a button right of Export… would move them; `screens.py`
512	  pins it ON, the first-run state the catalog shows, and lists the other three keys in
513	  `NOT_SHOWN`. The proof's live instances launch with `-FrameJobTips YES` or `NO`, so the owner's
514	  own toggle never decides a row. It holds twelve mutants, two past the usual ten, because the
515	  feature adds twelve separable decisions (two thresholds, the toggle, the month, the skip, the
516	  recorded ask, which queue states count, the agent's door, the button's and the pane's halves of
517	  the toggle, the success wiring and the order call) and dropping one would leave a decision no
518	  row is seen failing for.
519	---
520	title: Tips
521	description: What a tip pays for, where the Tips button is, when Frame Job asks by itself, and how to turn both off.
522	---
523	
524	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
525	
526	Frame Job is free to use and its source is open. It's made by one developer, and a tip helps pay for the time to keep working on it. Tipping is voluntary, and nothing in Frame Job is locked without one.
527	
528	<AtAGlance
529	  where="The green Tips button at the right end of the toolbar, and Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips"
530	/>
531	
532	## Leave a tip
533	
534	Click the green **Tips** button at the right end of the editor's toolbar, after **Export…**. A small window opens, titled Tips, that says who a tip pays for.
535	
536	| Button | What it does |
537	| --- | --- |
538	| **Leave a Tip** | Opens the tips page in your browser, then closes the window. <kbd>↩</kbd> presses it. |
539	| **Not Now** | Closes the window. <kbd>⎋</kbd> presses it, and so does the window's close button. |
540	
541	Frame Job takes no payment itself. The page in your browser does that, and Frame Job never learns whether you tipped.
542	
543	The same window opens from **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips**, with or without a project open. It isn't a sheet, so you can keep working with it open.
544	
545	## When Frame Job asks
546	
547	Frame Job opens the Tips window by itself a few times at most, and only just after an export you made has finished.
548	
549	- **The first time** comes once you've finished at least 5 exports and 30 days have passed since the first of them.
550	- **After that**, once a year, in December. If Frame Job asked, or you pressed **Leave a Tip**, after the start of June, it skips that year's December.
551	
552	It appears when you close the result of an **Export…**, or when an export you added to the queue finishes. It never takes the keyboard, so a key you were typing can't press one of its buttons. Close it and it won't come back until the next time it's due.
553	
554	Only exports you start from the export sheet count: **Export…** and **Add to Queue**. An export that fails or that you cancel doesn't count. Exports an agent or the Assistant starts don't count either, and they never open the window.
555	
556	Opening the window yourself and choosing **Not Now** changes nothing about when Frame Job next asks.
557	
558	## Turn tips off
559	
560	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** and find **Tips**, the last section.
561	
562	| Control | What it does | Default |
563	| --- | --- | --- |
564	| **Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder** | Shows the green **Tips** button in the toolbar and lets Frame Job open the Tips window by itself. Untick it to stop both. | On |
565	| **Tips** | Opens the Tips window. It's always there, whatever the box says. | |
566	
567	The box saves the moment you click it, and the button leaves or returns in every open editor window at once.
568	
569	## Good to know
570	
571	- Frame Job keeps the count of your exports, the date of the first one and the date it last asked in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, on your Mac only.
572	- December is judged by your Mac's time zone.
573	- If you export nothing in December, Frame Job doesn't ask that year.
574	- No agent tool opens the Tips window or changes this setting.
575	
576	## Related

579	- [The editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/#toolbar)

# Spec §11 — decisions: Tips

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

These were made with no road map, from the owner's words of 2026-11-14: a tips dialog, a green
Tips button to the right of Export in the editor, an automatic ask on a usage-then-calendar
schedule, and a Settings section that turns the ask and the button off. The owner called the
button an experiment that may be removed.

- **TIP-1 — A tip is voluntary, nothing in Frame Job is gated on one, and the app holds no payment
  code: the dialog says who a tip funds and opens one web page.** The statement is plain: Frame
  Job is made by one developer, it is free to use and its source is open, a tip helps pay for the
  time to keep working on it, and nothing is locked without one. "Leave a Tip" opens
  `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/` in the person's browser, and that address is ONE
  constant (`TipsLink.url`, `Tips.swift`), so moving the page is a one-line change. The page is
  the owner's to make. Frame Job never learns whether anyone tipped, so there is no "thank you"
  state and nothing to restore. Risk accepted: until the page exists the button opens a missing
  page.
- **TIP-2 — The dialog is its own small window titled "Tips", not a sheet and not an app-modal
  alert, and it has three doors: the editor's Tips button, Settings' Tips button and the automatic
  ask.** A sheet needs a host window and two of the doors have no document (Settings, and Settings
  opened from the Welcome window); an app-modal alert would stop every window and would sit in
  front of an MCP client's calls. A window that is modal to nothing cannot make anything wait. It
  is the Settings window's mould (`TipsWindowController`): one instance, not released when closed,
  no frame autosave name (so it writes no `NSWindow Frame` key), built from the sheets' own pieces
  (`makeSheetView`, `makeButtonRow`) so it reads as one of them, Escape on "Not Now" and Return on
  "Leave a Tip". It is left out of the Window menu: a two-button dialog is not a place to come
  back to, and both buttons reopen it. There is no menu item for it, and no MCP mirror, because
  showing it is not an edit (spec §7.9).
- **TIP-3 — The automatic ask is due by usage first and the calendar after: never while the
  toggle is off; first once at least 5 exports are counted AND at least 30 × 24 hours have passed
  since the first counted export; after an ask, only in a December, and a December is skipped
  whole when its 1 December 00:00 is less than six calendar months after the last ask.** The rule
  is one pure function, `TipsSchedule.isDue(_:now:calendar:)`, over the stored state, the moment
  and a calendar. "30 days of use" counts from the first counted export and not from the first
  launch: a launch is also what `framejob-mcp` and every proof make, and a date stamped at launch
  would count use by agents alone. It is elapsed time, not thirty separate days of use, which
  would make an occasional user wait a year. "December" is month 12 of the GREGORIAN calendar in
  the Mac's current time zone (`TipsSchedule.localCalendar()`, built at each evaluation), whatever
  calendar the person's Mac shows, so the same instant can be December in Auckland and November
  in Los Angeles. A December is judged whole so that an ask on 30 June cannot bring the next one
  on 30 December: a last ask after 1 June 00:00 skips that year's December, and one at or before
  it does not. A clock set back before the last ask or the first export makes nothing due. Risk
  accepted: the rule is evaluated only when a counted export completes (TIP-4), so a person who
  exports nothing in December is not asked that year.
- **TIP-4 — Only an export a person confirmed in the export card counts, and only its completion
  evaluates the ask; the agent's `export` never does either.** The card's two commits both sit
  behind its save panel (`ExportSheetCommit.swift`), which no tool and no dev switch answers:
  Export… (`EditorViewController.beginExport`) and Add to Queue (`enqueueExport`). The first hands
  the progress sheet an `onSuccess` it calls once, on a success only; the second follows its job
  by the id `enqueue` answered (`TipsQueueFollower`, `AgentExports`' pattern), so
  `ExportQueueController` is not changed and its jobs carry no origin. The agent's `export`
  enqueues on the same queue and is never followed, and the Assistant tab's `export` is that same
  door. So an instance driven only by an MCP client, the assistant or a proof counts nothing,
  writes no key and is never shown the dialog, which is what keeps `mcp.py`'s `DEFAULTS MOVED`
  guard quiet. A counted export is counted when it succeeds. The ask is evaluated, and recorded,
  at the moment it is shown: for Export…, when the result sheet ends (Close or Show in Finder),
  one main-queue turn later; for a queued job, when it completes. The automatic ask is ordered
  front WITHOUT becoming key, so a Return typed into the editor can never press "Leave a Tip";
  the two buttons' doors make it key. Risks accepted: after Show in Finder the dialog appears
  behind Finder and is found on return; a window closed with its result sheet still attached
  never ends that sheet, so that export is counted and the ask waits for the next one.
- **TIP-5 — The state is four keys of the bundle's defaults domain, written only at a person's
  doors.** `FrameJobTips` (Bool, absent means on) is the toggle, written by Settings' checkbox.
  `FrameJobTipsExports` (Int) and `FrameJobTipsFirstExport` (a date, stamped once) are written
  when a counted export succeeds, and counting goes on while the toggle is off, so turning it back
  on behaves sensibly. `FrameJobTipsLastAsked` (a date) is written when the automatic ask is shown
  and when "Leave a Tip" is pressed from any door: someone who has just visited the page is not
  asked again that December. Opening the dialog by hand and choosing "Not Now", or closing it,
  writes nothing. Dates are stored as dates, so `defaults write … -date` sets one. No project
  format changes. Risk accepted: the state is per Mac and per build identity, so a Debug build
  and a reinstall on another Mac each start again.
- **TIP-6 — The editor's Tips button is an `AccentButton` filled with `DS.tips` (`#2E7D32`), right
  of Export…, and Settings ▸ Tips holds the toggle that removes it.** The owner asked for green.
  The fill is a fixed leaf green, the same in both appearances as the recorder's coral Record
  button is, with the white `DS.onAccent` label at 5.1:1. It is deliberately not `DS.action` and
  not `DS.forest`: CI-4 keeps mint for the action ink and nothing else, and forest (`#1F8564`) is
  within 10/255 of the action ink's light value (`#1E8F6E`), so a forest button would read as an
  action in the light appearance. `DS.tips` sits about 40° of hue from both action values, so
  CI-4 stands unamended. How it looks is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`. The button is 12 pt
  after Export… with no rule between them, has no symbol, and is `TipsToolbarButton`, a view that
  hides itself while the toggle is off and follows `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`, so the
  frozen editor file holds nothing for it: removing the experiment is deleting that file and one
  line of `buildToolbar`. Settings' fifth and last pane, "Tips", is a bare heading, one visible
  sentence (under SH-5's and `settings_layout_probe` L5's 200 characters, so it needs no ⓘ), the
  checkbox "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder" (on by default) and a "Tips" button.
  Unticking stops the automatic ask and removes the button from every open editor at once; the
  pane's own button is never hidden or disabled and shows the dialog whatever the toggle says. It
  is a person's setting: no tool reads or writes it (R6-12, MC-7).
- **TIP-7 — The feature has no `-RCDev` switch and no dev tool, and its proof is a probe.**
  `tools/proof/tips_proof.py` builds `tips_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` and hands the schedule
  its clock, calendar and a scratch defaults suite; the two export doors are run for real, on a
  document made in process, with the ask, the window and the queue injected (`TipsDoors`), and the
  window's two order calls are closures so "front, not key" can be read where no probe window is
  ever key. A person pins state with `defaults write` (`docs/manual-checks.md`). So Debug, Release
  and Distribution run the same code. The offscreen harness pins `FrameJobTips` OFF: older chrome
  proofs read the toolbar at fixed points (`sharp_chrome.py`'s `EXPORT_RIGHT`,
  `phase7_chrome.py`'s accent patch) and a button right of Export… would move them; `screens.py`
  pins it ON, the first-run state the catalog shows, and lists the other three keys in
  `NOT_SHOWN`. The proof's live instances launch with `-FrameJobTips YES` or `NO`, so the owner's
  own toggle never decides a row. It holds twelve mutants, two past the usual ten, because the
  feature adds twelve separable decisions (two thresholds, the toggle, the month, the skip, the
  recorded ask, which queue states count, the agent's door, the button's and the pane's halves of
  the toggle, the success wiring and the order call) and dropping one would leave a decision no
  row is seen failing for.

title: Tips
description: What a tip pays for, where the Tips button is, when Frame Job asks by itself, and how to turn both off.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job is free to use and its source is open. It's made by one developer, and a tip helps pay for the time to keep working on it. Tipping is voluntary, and nothing in Frame Job is locked without one.

<AtAGlance
  where="The green Tips button at the right end of the toolbar, and Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips"
/>

## Leave a tip

Click the green **Tips** button at the right end of the editor's toolbar, after **Export…**. A small window opens, titled Tips, that says who a tip pays for.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Leave a Tip** | Opens the tips page in your browser, then closes the window. <kbd>↩</kbd> presses it. |
| **Not Now** | Closes the window. <kbd>⎋</kbd> presses it, and so does the window's close button. |

Frame Job takes no payment itself. The page in your browser does that, and Frame Job never learns whether you tipped.

The same window opens from **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips**, with or without a project open. It isn't a sheet, so you can keep working with it open.

## When Frame Job asks

Frame Job opens the Tips window by itself a few times at most, and only just after an export you made has finished.

- **The first time** comes once you've finished at least 5 exports and 30 days have passed since the first of them.
- **After that**, once a year, in December. If Frame Job asked, or you pressed **Leave a Tip**, after the start of June, it skips that year's December.

It appears when you close the result of an **Export…**, or when an export you added to the queue finishes. It never takes the keyboard, so a key you were typing can't press one of its buttons. Close it and it won't come back until the next time it's due.

Only exports you start from the export sheet count: **Export…** and **Add to Queue**. An export that fails or that you cancel doesn't count. Exports an agent or the Assistant starts don't count either, and they never open the window.

Opening the window yourself and choosing **Not Now** changes nothing about when Frame Job next asks.

## Turn tips off

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** and find **Tips**, the last section.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder** | Shows the green **Tips** button in the toolbar and lets Frame Job open the Tips window by itself. Untick it to stop both. | On |
| **Tips** | Opens the Tips window. It's always there, whatever the box says. | |

The box saves the moment you click it, and the button leaves or returns in every open editor window at once.

## Good to know

- Frame Job keeps the count of your exports, the date of the first one and the date it last asked in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, on your Mac only.
- December is judged by your Mac's time zone.
- If you export nothing in December, Frame Job doesn't ask that year.
- No agent tool opens the Tips window or changes this setting.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tips (spec §11 TIP-1…TIP-7) — the dialog, the editor's button, the automatic
ask and Settings' section.

    python3 tools/proof/tips_proof.py [--only ROW,…] [--no-live] [--mutant NAME]

A plain run builds `tips_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` through
`swift_build.build` and runs it once (B0, S, A, F, C, W), reads the tree's own
text (T1), then drives two instances of the app `RC_PROOF_APP` chooses over
MCP (L). `--no-live` leaves the L rows out. Every string and number a probe
row compares is a literal in the probe.

The probe (no app, nothing on screen, no browser, no real defaults domain):

  B0   the probe builds.
  S1   nothing recorded, and five exports with no first export: not due.
  S2   five exports: 29 d 23 h after the first is not due, 30 d after (1 July)
       is.
  S3   four exports after 400 d is not due; five is.
  S4   the toggle off with everything else due: not due.
  S5   after an ask on 10 February: 15 July no, 30 November 23:59:59 no,
       1 December 00:00:00 yes, 31 December 23:59:59 yes, 1 January no.
  S6   a last ask at 1 June 00:00:00 leaves that December due; at 00:00:01 it
       does not; one on 20 August skips that December and not the next.
  S7   asked on 5 December: 20 December no, 2 December a year on yes.
  S8   one instant, 2027-11-30T12:00Z: due in Pacific/Auckland (1 December
       there), not in America/Los_Angeles.
  S9   a clock set back: a day before the first export, and a December before
       the last ask, are not due.
  S10  `TipsSchedule.localCalendar()` is Gregorian in the current time zone;
       the constants are 30, 5 and 6.
  A1   `countExport` twice: 1 then 2, the first export stamped once.
  A2   `takeAsk` is false and writes nothing before it is due; due, it is true
       once, writes last-asked as the clock, and is false at once after.
  A3   the toggle off: written as `FrameJobTips` false with one post;
       `takeAsk` false and nothing written; a sixth export still counts.
  A4   `noteTipPageOpened` writes last-asked alone.
  A5   the four key names; an absent toggle reads on; both dates are stored as
       dates; the link is `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/`.
  F1   a followed job waiting, running, then completed: `completed` once over
       three settles.
  F2   a followed job cancelled, failed or removed: never, and dropped.
  F3   a completed job nobody followed: never; the followed one: once.
  C1   the dialog: its title, heading, body and hint; Not Now on Escape, Leave
       a Tip on Return; out of the Window menu, no frame autosave name;
       `show()` orders key and writes nothing; `showAutomatic()` orders front,
       never key; Not Now closes and writes nothing; Leave a Tip opens exactly
       the page, writes last-asked alone and closes. Its PNGs in both looks are
       written to `work/tips/…/scratch/` for a reader and checked for more
       than one colour only.
  C2   an in-process document's editor at 1440 pt and at the 900 pt minimum:
       the toolbar's row ends Export… then Tips; Tips is 12 pt after Export…
       and 12 pt from the edge, 26 pt tall at its own width; titled "Tips",
       fill #2E7D32, a nil-target `showTips:`, its tooltip; at 900 pt every
       control keeps its 1440 pt width and the spacer is wider than 0.
  C3   the toggle off (the argument domain, then the notification): the button
       is hidden and Export… is 12 pt from the edge; on again: back.
  C4   Settings' pane: heading, blurb, toggle, button; the literals; on by
       default; no info button; unticking writes `FrameJobTips` false and
       posts once; the Tips button is there, enabled, and shows the dialog in
       both states; the pane writes one key.
  W2   Export… through `EditorViewController.beginExport` on a state one
       export short of due: an export to a folder that is not there fails, and
       a cancelled one dismisses its sheet; neither counts, asks or orders the
       dialog.
  W1   the same door, a success: counted while the result sheet is still up,
       not asked; after Close the dialog is ordered front (never key) and
       last-asked is recorded; a second export counts and does not ask.
  W3   Add to Queue's door (`TipsDoors.follow`) on the probe's own queue: a
       job enqueued as the agent's is (unfollowed) and a followed one both
       complete, a followed third is cancelled while it waits; exactly one
       export is counted and the dialog is ordered front once.

The tree's text, read from the same sources the probe was built from:

  T1   `.exportSucceeded(` is called once, in `EditorViewController+Export.swift`;
       `.follow(queueJob:` is called once, there; `TipsDoors` is named in that
       file and `TipsWindowController.swift` alone; `.takeAsk(` and
       `.countExport(` are called in `TipsWindowController.swift` alone.

The app over MCP (`mcp.launch`, each instance stopped by its own pid):

  L0   `grep "Frame Job: "` of each instance's log prints nothing.
  L1   launched with `-FrameJobTips YES`: the toolbar capture's layout dump has
       a visible view reading "Tips" (`toolbar.tips`) right of the one reading
       "Export…"; the PNG is not one colour.
  L2   the same instance: an agent `export` of a one-clip project reaches
       `done`; `snapshot_ui`'s listing has no window titled "Tips" and
       `mcp.defaults_moved` is empty.
  L3   launched with `-FrameJobTips NO`: no visible view of the toolbar reads
       "Tips"; Settings' dump has the visible "Tips" button
       (`settings.tips.button`) and the toggle's title.

Mutants (`--mutant`), each a literal found exactly once in a copy of
`app/Sources`, which the probe is rebuilt over (L rows never run):

  days-ignored          the 30-day guard removed: must fail S2.
  exports-ignored       the five-export guard removed: must fail S3.
  toggle-ignored        the schedule ignores the toggle: must fail S4, A3.
  any-month             any month counts as December: must fail S5.
  skip-ignored          no December is skipped: must fail S6, S7.

def resources(here):
    """What W1–W3's real exports read beside the binary, as the app reads them
    from its bundle: `default.metallib`, compiled from the tree's shaders, and
    `Blank.mp4`, the placeholder track of a timeline with no media. None, or
    why one could not be made."""
    airs = []
    for shader in sorted(SHADERS.glob("*.metal")):
        air = here / (shader.stem + ".air")
        step = subprocess.run(
            ["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c", str(shader), "-o", str(air)],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        if step.returncode:
            return f"metal {shader.name}: {step.stderr[:300]}"
        airs.append(str(air))
    step = subprocess.run(
        ["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", *airs, "-o", str(here / "default.metallib")],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
    if step.returncode:
        return f"metallib: {step.stderr[:300]}"
    shutil.copyfile(ROOT / "app/Resources/Blank.mp4", here / "Blank.mp4")
    return None


def build(sources, here):
    """(binary, None) or (None, why): `swift_build.build`, without the
    dev-tools flag (nothing here needs it), with `resources` beside it."""
    why = resources(here)
    if why:
        return None, why
    entry = here / "main.swift"
    shutil.copyfile(HERE / "tips_probe.swift", entry)
    binary = here / "tips-probe"
    swift = sorted(str(p) for p in sources.glob("*.swift") if p.name != "main.swift")
    if len(swift) < 100:
        return None, "app source set incomplete"
    try:
        swift_build.build(sources=swift + [entry], output=binary)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        return None, "swiftc: " + "; ".join(error.diagnostics[:8])
    return binary, None


def mutate(sources, name, dest):
    """A copy of `sources` with the mutant's edits; None, or why when a
    `before` text is not found exactly once."""
    shutil.copytree(sources, dest)
    for file, before, after in MUTANTS[name][1]:
        path = dest / file
        text = path.read_text() if path.exists() else ""
        if text.count(before) != 1:
            return f"{file}: `{before}` found {text.count(before)} times"
        path.write_text(text.replace(before, after))
    return None


def probe(binary, here):
    """(the probe's answer, None), or (None, why)."""
    scratch = here / "scratch"
    home = here / "home"
    scratch.mkdir()
    home.mkdir()
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [str(binary), str(scratch), str(ROOT / "app/Resources/Fonts")],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=WALL, cwd=here, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            env=bounded.child_env({"CFFIXED_USER_HOME": str(home)}))
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return None, f"no answer within {WALL} s"
    (here / "stderr.txt").write_text(result.stderr)
    try:
        answer = json.loads(result.stdout)
        answer["rows"]
        return answer, None
    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
        return None, f"no answer (exit {result.returncode}): {result.stderr[-400:]}"


# ---- T1: the tree's text ----------------------------------------------------------

def tree_row(sources):
    texts = {p.name: p.read_text() for p in sorted(sources.glob("*.swift"))}

    def files(needle):
        return sorted(name for name, text in texts.items() if needle in text)

    def count(needle):
        return sum(text.count(needle) for text in texts.values())

    facts = [
        (".exportSucceeded( is called once, in the export door",
         count(".exportSucceeded(") == 1 and files(".exportSucceeded(") == [DOOR]),
        (".follow(queueJob: is called once, in the export door",
         count(".follow(queueJob:") == 1 and files(".follow(queueJob:") == [DOOR]),
        ("TipsDoors is named in the export door and its own file alone",
         files("TipsDoors") == sorted([DOOR, WINDOW])),
        (".takeAsk( is called in the Tips window's file alone", files(".takeAsk(") == [WINDOW]),
        (".countExport( is called in the Tips window's file alone",
         files(".countExport(") == [WINDOW]),
    ]
    detail = "; ".join(f"{name} {ok}" for name, ok in facts)
    detail += (f" (exportSucceeded in {files('.exportSucceeded(')}, follow in "
               f"{files('.follow(queueJob:')}, TipsDoors in {files('TipsDoors')})")
    return all(ok for _, ok in facts), detail


# ---- L: the app over MCP ----------------------------------------------------------

def png_colours(path):
    """How many distinct byte values the PNG's inflated image data holds; 0
    when it cannot be read. One colour inflates to a handful."""
    try:
        data = Path(path).read_bytes()
        at, chunks = 8, []
        while at + 8 <= len(data):
            length = int.from_bytes(data[at:at + 4], "big")
            if data[at + 4:at + 8] == b"IDAT":
                chunks.append(data[at + 8:at + 8 + length])
            at += 12 + length
        return len(set(zlib.decompress(b"".join(chunks))))
    except Exception:  # an unreadable capture is a failed row, not a crash
        return 0


def views_of(answer):
    with open(answer["layout_path"]) as handle:
        return json.load(handle)["views"]


def shown(views, text=None, ident=None):
    return [v for v in views if not v.get("hidden")
            and (text is None or v.get("text") == text)
            and (ident is None or v.get("id") == ident)]


def instance(binary, tag, toggle, session, results, body):
    """One instance with `-FrameJobTips <toggle>`; its parity line joins L0."""
    log = session / f"{tag}.log"
    home = session / f"home-{tag}"
    home.mkdir(parents=True)
    arguments = ["-NSRecentDocumentsLimit", "0", "-FrameJobTips", toggle]
    launched = mcp.launch(str(binary), arguments=arguments,
                          env=bounded.child_env({"CFFIXED_USER_HOME": str(home)}),
                          log_path=str(log), timeout=CALL_BOUND)
    try:
        if launched.client is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"the instance did not listen (log {log})")
        print(f"  {tag}: instance PID {launched.child.pid}", flush=True)
        body(launched)
    finally:
        launched.stop()
        try:
            lines = [line.strip() for line in open(log, errors="replace")
                     if "Frame Job: " in line]
        except OSError:
            lines = [f"{log} could not be read"]
        results.setdefault("parity", []).append((tag, lines))
        mcp.remove_scratch(launched.socket_path)


def live(wanted):
    results = {}
    answers = {}
    session = WORK / "live"
    if session.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(session)
    out = session / "out"
    out.mkdir(parents=True)

    def fail_all(why):
        for row in LIVE_ROWS:
            answers.setdefault(row, (False, why))

    try:
        binary = proof_app.executable(proof_app.bundle())
    except Exception as error:  # no app is every live row's failure
        fail_all(f"no app: {error}")
        return answers

    def toolbar(client, project, name):
        return client.call_with("snapshot_ui", {
            "project": project, "window": "editor", "view": "toolbar",
            "path": str(out / name), "fill_preview": False})

    def on(launched):
        client = launched.client
        project = str(session / "on.framejob")
        client.call_with("new_project", {"path": project})
        answer = toolbar(client, project, "toolbar-on.png")
        views = views_of(answer)
        tips = shown(views, text="Tips", ident="toolbar.tips")
        export = shown(views, text="Export…")
        colours = png_colours(out / "toolbar-on.png")
        right = bool(tips and export
                     and tips[0]["frame"][0] >= export[0]["frame"][0] + export[0]["frame"][2])
        answers["L1"] = (
            len(tips) == 1 and len(export) == 1 and right and colours > 8,
            f"visible Tips views {[v['frame'] for v in tips]}, Export… "
            f"{[v['frame'] for v in export]}, Tips right of Export… {right}; the PNG's data "
            f"holds {colours} byte values")

        got = client.call_with("get_project", {"project": project})["project"]
        client.call_with("add_shape_clip", {
            "project": project, "track": got["tracks"][0]["id"], "at": 0, "duration": 600000})
        done = client.export_with(
            {"project": project, "preset": "h264", "path": str(out / "agent.mp4")},
            seconds=CALL_BOUND)
        listing = client.call_with("snapshot_ui", {})
        titles = [w.get("title") for w in listing.get("windows", [])]
        moved = mcp.defaults_moved(launched.socket_path)
        answers["L2"] = (
            isinstance(done, dict) and (out / "agent.mp4").exists() and "Tips" not in titles
            and moved == [],
            f"export answered {done.get('status') if isinstance(done, dict) else done!r}, the "
            f"file exists {(out / 'agent.mp4').exists()}; visible windows {titles}; defaults "
            f"moved {moved}")
        client.call_with("close_project", {"project": project, "discard": True})

    def off(launched):
        client = launched.client
        project = str(session / "off.framejob")
        client.call_with("new_project", {"path": project})
        views = views_of(toolbar(client, project, "toolbar-off.png"))
        tips = shown(views, text="Tips")
        export = shown(views, text="Export…")
        client.call_with("perform_menu_item", {"path": ["Frame Job", "Settings…"]})
        settings = views_of(client.call_with("snapshot_ui", {
            "window": "settings", "path": str(out / "settings-off.png")}))
        button = shown(settings, text="Tips", ident="settings.tips.button")
        toggle = shown(settings, text="Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder",
                       ident="settings.tips.toggle")
        answers["L3"] = (
            not tips and len(export) == 1 and len(button) == 1 and len(toggle) == 1,
            f"toolbar views reading Tips {len(tips)}, Export… {len(export)}; Settings' Tips "
            f"button {len(button)}, toggle {len(toggle)}")
        client.call_with("close_project", {"project": project, "discard": True})

            continue

            instance(binary, tag, toggle, session, results, body)
        except Exception as error:  # a row that could not run is that row's failure
            for row in rows:

    answers["L0"] = (
        len(parity) > 0 and all(not lines for _, lines in parity),
        "; ".join(f"{tag}: {lines[:2] or 'nothing'}" for tag, lines in parity) or "no instance ran")
    fail_all("not run")
    return answers


# ---- the run ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--sources", type=Path, default=ROOT / "app/Sources")
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", choices=sorted(MUTANTS))
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated row ids")
    parser.add_argument("--no-live", action="store_true", help="leave the L rows out")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    named = MUTANTS[args.mutant][0] if args.mutant else []
    if args.only:
        wanted = args.only.split(",")
    elif args.mutant:
        wanted = ["B0"] + named
    else:
        wanted = [row for row in ROWS if not (args.no_live and row in LIVE_ROWS)]
    unknown = [row for row in wanted if row not in ROWS]
    if unknown:
        print("unknown row " + ", ".join(unknown))
        return 2
    if args.mutant and set(wanted) & set(LIVE_ROWS):
        print("a mutant is a probe rebuild; the L rows do not run under one")
        return 2
    here = WORK / (f"mutant-{args.mutant}" if args.mutant else "tree")
    if here.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(here)
    here.mkdir(parents=True)
    sources = args.sources.resolve()
    if args.mutant:
        why = mutate(sources, args.mutant, here / "Sources")
        if why:
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — {why}")
            return 2
        sources = here / "Sources"

    results = {}
    not_scored = []
    probe_wanted = [row for row in wanted if row in PROBE_ROWS]
    if "B0" in wanted or probe_wanted:
        binary, why = build(sources, here)
        results["B0"] = (binary is not None, why or f"built from {sources}")
        if binary is None and args.mutant:
            print(f"B0 fail — {why}")
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — the copy did "
                  "not build")
            return 2
        if probe_wanted:
            if binary is None:
                for row in probe_wanted:
                    results[row] = (False, "not run: the probe did not build")
            else:
                answer, why = probe(binary, here)
                rows = (answer or {}).get("rows") or []
                for row in probe_wanted:
                    found = next((a for a in rows if a.get("id") == row), None)
                    if found is None:
                        not_scored.append(row)
                        results[row] = (False, f"no row: {why or 'the probe did not answer it'}")
                    else:
                        results[row] = (bool(found["pass"]), found["detail"])
    if "T1" in wanted:
        results["T1"] = tree_row(sources)
    if set(wanted) & set(LIVE_ROWS):
        results.update(live(wanted))

    for row in wanted:
        good, detail = results[row]
        print(f"{row} {'pass' if good else 'fail'} — {detail}")
    passed = sum(1 for row in wanted if results[row][0])
    print(f"scores: {passed}/{len(wanted)}")
    if not args.mutant:
        return 0 if passed == len(wanted) else 1
    lost = [row for row in named if row in not_scored or row not in results]
    if lost:
        print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — "
              f"{', '.join(lost)} not scored")
        return 2
    survived = [row for row in named if results[row][0]]
    if survived:
        print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: SURVIVED — {', '.join(survived)} passed")
        return 0
    print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: CAUGHT — {', '.join(named)} failed")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
